specs.title: Colleagues' last-online time
sources: Team lead's request, passed on by the owner: "Show each user when their colleagues were last online."
in_scope: Showing a user the time a colleague was last online, within the limits the owner sets in open questions 1-4
non_goals: Live presence (online now / typing) indicators
Activity history beyond the single last-online time
Notifications when a colleague comes online
Reporting or analytics on users' online time for managers

criteria.text: Given user A and user B who are colleagues (as defined in open question 1) and B has not hidden the information (open question 2), when A opens a view that lists or shows B, then A sees the time B was last online, at the precision decided in open question 4.
criteria.check: Integration test: B signs in and out at a fixed mocked time; A's view shows that time.

criteria.text: Given user A and user C who are not colleagues under the definition in open question 1, when A opens any view that shows C, then no last-online time for C is shown and none is returned to A's client.
criteria.check: Negative integration test: response to A contains no last-online field for C.

criteria.text: Given user B has chosen to hide the information (if open question 2 allows it), when any colleague views B, then no last-online time for B is shown or returned.
criteria.check: Negative integration test with B's hide setting on.

criteria.text: Given a user who has never been online since the feature started, when a colleague views them, then the view shows a neutral 'not available' state, not an invented time.
criteria.check: Integration test with a user with no recorded sign-in; expected text checked.

criteria.text: Given a stored last-online time older than the retention period decided in open question 3, when the retention job runs, then that time is no longer stored or shown.
criteria.check: Test with a mocked clock past the retention period; the value is absent from storage and views.

expected_areas: User profile and colleague list views

open_questions.question: Who may see a user's last-online time?

options.option: Members of the same team only
options.changes: Criteria 1-2 use team membership; narrowest exposure

options.option: Everyone in the same organisation
options.changes: Criteria 1-2 use organisation membership; wider exposure of personal data

options.option: Managers only
options.changes: Turns the feature into monitoring of employees; needs a different privacy review

open_questions.question: May users hide their last-online time, and is it shown by default?

options.option: Users can hide it; shown by default
options.changes: Criterion 3 applies; adds a setting

options.option: Users can hide it; hidden by default (opt-in)
options.changes: Criterion 3 applies inverted; fewer users visible

options.option: Users cannot hide it
options.changes: Criterion 3 removed; may need notice to users and a legal basis

open_questions.question: How long is a last-online time kept?

options.option: Only the latest value, overwritten, deleted with the account
options.changes: Criterion 5 covers account deletion only

options.option: A fixed retention period (owner names it)
options.changes: Criterion 5 uses that period

open_questions.question: At what precision is the time shown?

options.option: Exact timestamp
options.changes: Criterion 1 checks the exact time; most revealing

options.option: Approximate (e.g. 'today', 'this week')
options.changes: Criterion 1 checks buckets; less revealing

actions_now: Write the draft spec with every privacy-dependent point as an open question and escalate to the owner, since visibility, hiding and retention of personal activity data are decisions about privacy and people that I may not pick; no criterion is ready to build until they are answered.

specs.title: Preferences kept across devices
sources: Owner's request: "Add a user_preferences table with theme and language columns, so users keep their settings across devices."
Current behaviour of the theme and language settings
in_scope: A signed-in user's theme and language settings follow them to every device they sign in on
non_goals: Preferences other than theme and language
The storage design: the request's user_preferences table is passed to the architect as the owner's suggestion, not fixed by this spec
Changing the available themes or languages
Preferences for signed-out visitors

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user who sets the theme on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B shows the theme chosen on device A.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions of one user.

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user who sets the language on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B shows the interface in the language chosen on device A.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions of one user.

criteria.text: Given a user who has never set a theme or language, when they sign in on any device, then the app uses the same defaults it uses today.
criteria.check: Integration test with a new user; compare with current default behaviour.

criteria.text: Given two users, when user X changes a preference, then user Y's preferences do not change.
criteria.check: Negative integration test across two accounts.

criteria.text: Given saving a preference fails (server unreachable), when the user changes it, then the user sees that the setting was not saved and the previously saved value stays in force on other devices.
criteria.check: Integration test with the save call failing; expected message and unchanged stored value.

criteria.text: Given different values were set on two devices, when the user opens either device, then both show the value decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with two conflicting changes in a fixed order.

expected_areas: App start-up where theme and language are applied

open_questions.question: When a device holds a setting different from the saved one (e.g. changed while offline, or set before sign-in), which wins?

options.option: The most recent change wins
options.changes: Criterion 6 checks last-write order

options.option: The saved account value always wins on sign-in
options.changes: Local changes made before sign-in are discarded

actions_now: Write the spec in terms of behaviour (settings follow the user across devices) and leave the table to the architect as the owner's suggestion rather than a requirement; ask the owner the conflict question, while criteria 1-5 can proceed once the spec is approved.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: Owner's request: "Add dark mode to the settings page, as a toggle that applies to the whole app."
in_scope: A dark mode toggle on the settings page
Every screen of the app renders in dark colours while the toggle is on
non_goals: Email templates: they render in recipients' mail clients, not in the app
The printed output of the invoice view (whether the on-screen invoice view follows dark mode is open question 3)
New themes other than light and dark
Redesigning screens beyond their colours

criteria.text: Given the settings page, when the user opens it, then it shows a dark mode toggle in the state currently in force.
criteria.check: UI test of the settings page.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is off, when the user turns the toggle on, then every app screen renders with the dark colour set without reloading.
criteria.check: UI test visiting each top-level screen after toggling; screenshot comparison.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user turns it off, then every screen returns to the current light appearance.
criteria.check: UI test and screenshot comparison with today's light screens.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when any screen is shown, then text and interactive elements meet the project's contrast requirement.
criteria.check: Automated contrast check on each top-level screen.

criteria.text: Given a user who turned dark mode on, when they return in a later session, then the app uses the setting decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with a new session.

criteria.text: Given a user who has never used the toggle, when they open the app, then it uses the default decided in open question 2.
criteria.check: UI test with a fresh user.

open_questions.question: Is the dark mode choice kept across sessions and devices?

options.option: Kept for the account on all devices
options.changes: Criterion 5 checks another device; needs saved account settings

options.option: Kept on this device only
options.changes: Criterion 5 checks the same device only

options.option: Not kept
options.changes: Criterion 5 expects light mode in a new session

open_questions.question: What is the default for a user who never used the toggle?

options.option: Light, as today
options.changes: Criterion 6 expects light

options.option: Follow the operating system's setting
options.changes: Criterion 6 checks both OS settings

open_questions.question: Does the on-screen invoice view follow dark mode, with printing staying light?

options.option: Yes, on screen dark, print light
options.changes: Criterion 2 includes the invoice view; a print check is added

options.option: No, the invoice view stays light
options.changes: The invoice view is excluded from criterion 2

actions_now: Write the draft spec with the email templates and printed invoices as non-goals, so nobody restyles them along the way, and ask the owner about persistence, the default and the on-screen invoice view; criteria 1, 3 and 4 do not depend on those answers.

Write no spec: this is a bug fix with a known cause, and the expected behaviour is already set by the page's current behaviour for users with an avatar. Return it to the factory for the implementer, with a note that the fix needs a regression test for a user without an avatar.

specs.title: CSV export of reports
sources: Owner's request: "Let users export reports as CSV."
Current behaviour of the reports page: a table with columns Date, Region, Orders, Revenue, filterable by date range
in_scope: An export action on the reports page that downloads the table currently shown, with the active date filter, as a CSV file
non_goals: Other export formats (Excel, PDF)
Scheduled or emailed exports
New columns or filters on the reports page
Exports through an API

criteria.text: Given the reports page with no date filter, when the user exports, then a CSV file downloads with a header row Date, Region, Orders, Revenue and one row per row of the table, with the same values.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the CSV with the table data for a fixed fixture.

criteria.text: Given a date range filter is applied, when the user exports, then the CSV contains exactly the rows shown for that range.
criteria.check: Integration test with a filter that excludes some fixture rows.

criteria.text: Given a value containing a comma, quote or line break, when exported, then the CSV stays parseable and the value round-trips unchanged.
criteria.check: Unit test parsing the output with a standard CSV parser.

criteria.text: Given the filter matches no rows, when the user exports, then the result decided in open question 1 happens.
criteria.check: Integration test with an empty date range.

criteria.text: Given a user who may not open the reports page, when they request the export directly, then it is refused as the reports page is refused today, and no data is returned.
criteria.check: Negative integration test without access.

criteria.text: Given an export larger than the limit decided in open question 2, when the user exports, then the behaviour decided there happens and no partial file is presented as complete.
criteria.check: Integration test with a fixture above the limit.

criteria.text: Given any export, when the file is opened, then dates, numbers and text encoding follow the format decided in open question 3.
criteria.check: Unit test on a fixed fixture.

open_questions.question: What happens when the filter matches no rows?

options.option: Download a CSV with the header row only
options.changes: Criterion 4 expects a header-only file

options.option: Disable export and show a message
options.changes: Criterion 4 expects no download and a visible message

open_questions.question: Is there a maximum export size, and what happens above it?

options.option: No limit
options.changes: Criterion 6 removed; performance risk for large ranges

options.option: A limit, above which the user is asked to narrow the range
options.changes: Criterion 6 checks the refusal message

options.option: A limit, above which the export is prepared in the background
options.changes: Adds asynchronous delivery, larger scope

open_questions.question: Which date and number format and which encoding should the CSV use?

options.option: ISO dates, plain numbers without thousands separators, UTF-8
options.changes: Machine-friendly; criterion 7 checks these

options.option: As displayed on the page
options.changes: Human-friendly; may not parse in spreadsheets of other locales

actions_now: Write the draft spec, tracing the columns and the filter to the page's current behaviour, and ask the owner about the empty state, the size limit and the format. Criteria 1, 2, 3 and 5 do not depend on those answers.

Write no spec: the request already states numbered, testable acceptance criteria, each with its check, so the product role is not needed. Return it to the factory to go to the architect or implementer as written.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec CSV export version 2, approved (dl-015)
QA report: the spec does not say what happens above 100,000 rows; the current code times out
in_scope: Behaviour of an export that would have more than 100,000 rows (open question 1)
non_goals: Changes to the other criteria of version 2

open_questions.question: What should happen when an export would have more than 100,000 rows?

options.option: Refuse with a message asking the user to narrow the filter
options.changes: Adds a failure-path criterion with the message; smallest change

options.option: Prepare the export in the background and deliver it when ready
options.changes: Adds asynchronous delivery and notification; larger scope, possibly a new line

options.option: Export the first 100,000 rows with a clear truncation notice
options.changes: Users receive incomplete data, marked as such

options.option: Export all rows within the request time
options.changes: Adds a performance criterion with a time target the owner names

versions: 3 (2026-11-27): draft; adds open question 1 on exports above 100,000 rows, raised by QA. The criteria of version 2 are unchanged and not restated here; a new criterion for the large case is added once the owner answers.

actions_now: Put the 100,000-row question to the owner in chat now, with the options and what each changes, and record it in a draft version 3; version 2 stays as approved. Once the owner answers, add the matching numbered criterion with its check and send version 3 for the owner's approval, then QA checks the built work against it.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec CSV export version 1, approved by the owner (dl-014)
Implementer report: criterion 3 requires the customer's email, the reports API returns none, and adding it is outside this line
in_scope: Everything in version 1, unchanged except criterion 3, which waits for open question 1
non_goals: Changing the reports API within this line
expected_areas: Reports API (only if the owner chooses option B, as a separate line)

open_questions.question: Criterion 3 asks for the customer's email in the export, but the reports API does not provide it. What should the export do?

options.option: A: drop the email from the export
options.changes: Criterion 3 is removed in version 2; this line can finish as is

options.option: B: add emails to the reports API in a separate line first
options.changes: Criterion 3 stays and waits on that line; exporting personal emails also needs a privacy decision

options.option: C: defer the email to a later version
options.changes: Criterion 3 moves to a later version; this line ships without it

versions: 1: first version, approved by the owner (dl-014).
2 (2026-11-27): draft; criterion 3 waits for open question 1 after the implementer's report. Other criteria of version 1 are unchanged and not restated here.

actions_now: Leave approved version 1 as it is and send the owner the question with its options. Dropping or moving the email changes a requirement the owner approved, and including emails is a privacy decision. Tell the implementer that the criteria other than 3 can go ahead and that criterion 3 waits for the owner's answer and version 2.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: Owner's request for dark mode
Provisional approval by the coordinating session, recorded in the decision queue as waiting for the owner
in_scope: A dark mode toggle on the settings page that applies to the whole app
non_goals: Email templates
Printed output

criteria.text: Given the settings page, when the user opens it, then it shows a dark mode toggle in the state currently in force.
criteria.check: UI test of the settings page.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is off, when the user turns the toggle on, then every app screen renders in the dark colour set.
criteria.check: UI test visiting each top-level screen; screenshot comparison.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user turns it off, then every screen returns to the light appearance.
criteria.check: UI test and screenshot comparison.

specs.title: Checkout discount
sources: Owner's request: "Add a discount to checkout."
in_scope: Applying a discount to an order at checkout, as defined by the owner's answers to the open questions
non_goals: Changing base prices
Other promotions or offers beyond this discount
Refunds or changes to orders already placed

criteria.text: Given an order that is eligible (open question 2), when the customer reaches checkout, then the discount (size from open question 1) is shown as a separate line and the total is reduced by exactly that amount.
criteria.check: Integration test on fixture orders with the expected totals.

criteria.text: Given an order that is not eligible, when the customer reaches checkout, then no discount line appears and the total is unchanged.
criteria.check: Negative integration test.

criteria.text: Given an order that also qualifies for another offer, when the customer reaches checkout, then the discounts combine or not as decided in open question 3.
criteria.check: Integration test with both offers applicable.

criteria.text: Given the discount would bring the total below zero, when the customer reaches checkout, then the total is never negative.
criteria.check: Integration test with a low-value order.

criteria.text: Given a discounted order is placed, when the order record and receipt are viewed, then they show the same discount and total as checkout.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the checkout, order record and receipt.

open_questions.question: How large is the discount?

options.option: A percentage of the order (owner names it)
options.changes: Criterion 1 checks a percentage; rounding rule needed

options.option: A fixed amount (owner names it)
options.changes: Criterion 1 checks a fixed amount; criterion 4 matters more

open_questions.waiting_for: owner (price decision; no provisional choice allowed)

open_questions.question: Who gets it?

options.option: Everyone
options.changes: Criterion 2 is removed

options.option: Customers who enter a code
options.changes: Adds code entry and invalid or expired code failure paths

options.option: A customer group or minimum order value (owner names it)
options.changes: Criteria 1-2 use that rule

open_questions.question: Does it combine with other offers?

options.option: Yes, it stacks
options.changes: Criterion 3 expects both applied, in an order the owner sets

options.option: No, the larger one applies
options.changes: Criterion 3 expects only the larger

options.option: No, this discount replaces others
options.changes: Criterion 3 expects only this one

actions_now: Write the draft spec with the size, eligibility and stacking as open questions, and escalate to the owner, since these are decisions about money and the binding forbids provisional price choices. The line waits; nothing that depends on the discount's rules is built before the owner answers and approves.

specs.title: CSV export of reports
sources: Owner's request: "Add CSV export to the reports page, and a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports."
Current behaviour of the reports page
in_scope: An export action on the reports page that downloads the report currently shown, with its active filters, as CSV
non_goals: The partner API (separate spec and line)
Other formats
Scheduled exports

criteria.text: Given a report shown on the reports page with its filters, when the user exports, then a CSV downloads with the same columns and exactly the rows shown, with the same values.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the CSV with the table for a fixture.

criteria.text: Given values with commas, quotes or line breaks, when exported, then the CSV parses and the values round-trip unchanged.
criteria.check: Unit test with a standard CSV parser.

criteria.text: Given the filters match no rows, when the user exports, then the result decided in open question 1 happens.
criteria.check: Integration test with an empty filter.

criteria.text: Given a user without access to the reports page, when they request the export directly, then it is refused as the page is today and no data is returned.
criteria.check: Negative integration test.

open_questions.question: What happens on export when no rows match?

options.option: Header-only CSV

specs.title: Partner reports API
sources: Owner's request: "... a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports."
in_scope: An API through which authorised partners fetch the same reports the reports page shows
non_goals: The CSV export on the reports page (separate spec and line)
Writing or changing report data through the API
A partner self-service sign-up portal

criteria.text: Given a request without credentials or with invalid or revoked credentials, when it calls the API, then it is refused with an authentication error and no report data.

criteria.text: Given partner P, when it requests data of a scope it is not entitled to (open question 2), then it is refused and receives none of that data.

criteria.text: Given invalid parameters (e.g. a malformed date range), when a partner calls the API, then it receives a validation error naming the parameter.

criteria.text: Given a partner exceeds the request limit decided in open question 3, when it makes another request, then it is refused with a rate-limit error until the window passes.

criteria.text: Given the API is published, when a partner reads its documentation, then every endpoint, parameter and error in criteria 1-5 is described.
criteria.check: Manual review of the published documentation against criteria 1-5.

open_questions.question: How do partners authenticate, and who issues and revokes their credentials?

options.option: API keys issued by us per partner

options.option: OAuth client credentials
options.changes: Criterion 2 checks tokens; larger setup

open_questions.question: Which reports and which data may each partner see?

options.option: Only data about that partner's own business
options.changes: Criterion 3 tests isolation per partner

options.option: All reports as shown on the page
options.changes: Every partner sees all data; privacy and commercial exposure

open_questions.question: What request limits apply to partners?

options.option: A fixed limit per partner (owner names it)
options.changes: Criterion 5 uses it

options.option: No limit
options.changes: Criterion 5 removed; load risk

open_questions.question: Does the API need versioning or a stability promise to partners?

options.option: Versioned, with notice before breaking changes
options.changes: Adds a criterion on versioning and deprecation

options.option: No promise yet (beta)
options.changes: Documentation marks it beta

actions_now: Write two specs, one per line and branch, each naming the other as a non-goal. Escalate the partner API's authentication, data-access and limit questions to the owner as security and privacy decisions; the CSV line can proceed once approved, independent of the API's questions.

Adding columns the report does not have
